text: Code refactoring is the process of improving your code's structure without changing what it actually does. It's like tidying up a messy room—you're not buying new furniture, just arranging things more logically. The main goal is to make the code more readable and maintainable. When you refactor, you break long functions into smaller ones, remove duplicate code, and improve variable names. This reduces what developers call "technical debt", which is the accumulated cost of quick fixes and messy code. While refactoring doesn't add new features, it makes future changes faster and safer. Clean, well-structured code is easier to understand, test, and modify, saving time and frustration in the long run.
